who-this-is-for.text: This page is for a holder of an active name who wants to change its payment destination, recover after losing the current controller, or retire permanently. The complete playable lifecycle replays thirty-eight Lean-derived rows and then drives the same public transition in the browser. Maintenance and recovery keep the representative in application custody. Retirement moves it into completion-only custody before burning it. This remains design-time evidence, not ledger execution.

change-the-payment-destination.text: The controller may set, replace, or clear one optional payment destination. The destination is routing data, not authority. The sequence keeps the registry identity, key, representative, controller, next commitment, and quorum unchanged, and makes no registry request, mint, or burn. Wrong authority, multiple destinations, and control-field tampering are refused.

recover-with-the-committed-next-controll.text: Recovery reveals the complete next controller address, checks its canonical bytes against the domain-separated BLAKE two b two hundred and fifty six commitment, and requires its payment-key signer. The old controller need not sign. The successor keeps the representative, installs the revealed controller, and stores a fresh commitment. Only canonical base and enterprise payment-key addresses are supported.

retire-permanently.text: Either the controller or a sufficient retirement quorum initiates retirement. The quorum is a retirement authorization, not next-controller recovery and not a death oracle. Both routes put the representative into one completion-only request. Permissionless folding burns it and moves the key to Over. Pending retirement remains distinct from Over, and withdrawal, redirection, replay, Delete, release, and re-registration are refused. Retirement prevents name-based resolution, but cannot stop a direct send to a previously saved raw Cardano address.

what-remains-deliberately-unavailable.text: Cancelling an unfulfilled naming claim remains on hold. Insert certification never grants cancellation permission, but the signer, refund recipient, refund value, and fee treatment are undecided. The naming interface therefore offers no claim-cancellation button or success claim. Retirement-request withdrawal is different: it is a required refusal attempt. The generic registry demonstration is not naming policy.

consumer-and-ledger-boundary.text: The consumer contract is source-bound to a pinned cardano KERI commit. It uses Conway inline-datum and required-signer precedents without importing KERI schemas or claiming compiled-script interoperability. Singular publishes its own wire indices and field order, binds one registry identity per application, and rejects a rival initialization seed. The table separates what existing tooling constrains, what Singular publishes, and what remains outside the candidate.

evidence-and-release-status.text: The browser drives integrated maintenance, recovery, and both retirement routes with their refusals. Retirement is queued first, showing pending, and completed by a separate permissionless fold, showing retired or Over. The reconciliation table binds all thirty-eight model and corpus identities to public controls and assertions. The downloadable archive carries raw model, contract, scenarios, replay sources, pinned tooling, and exact identities under one SHA two hundred and fifty six manifest. This is still an unaccepted design candidate, not a deployed validator or ledger observation.
